about: Spec cards (docs/walkthrough-design.md section 2.2h). Each row names a spec as it appears on screen. Its title and link come from the glossary.json source it names, so each URL is written once. specParts finds the names and aliases at render, longest first.

specs.name: FIPS 46-3
specs.synopsis: The US standard for DES, a block cipher with a 56-bit key. NIST withdrew it in 2005, because a 56-bit key is too short.

specs.name: FIPS 180-4
specs.synopsis: The US standard for the SHA-1 and SHA-2 hash functions, which include SHA-256. It gives the padding and the rounds.

specs.name: FIPS 186-5
specs.synopsis: The US standard for digital signatures: RSA, ECDSA and EdDSA, which includes Ed25519.

specs.name: FIPS 198-1
specs.synopsis: The US standard for HMAC, a seal on a message made from a hash function and a secret key.

specs.name: FIPS 203
specs.synopsis: The US standard for ML-KEM, a way for two sides to agree a shared key. It is designed to resist attacks by quantum computers.

specs.name: SP 800-38A
specs.synopsis: NIST's guide to five modes for a block cipher: ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB and CTR.

specs.name: SP 800-38D
specs.synopsis: NIST's guide to GCM, a mode that locks data and seals it with a tag in one pass.

specs.name: SP 800-57
specs.synopsis: NIST's guide to key management. Part 1 lists the strength in bits that each key size gives.

specs.name: SP 800-67 Rev. 2
specs.synopsis: NIST's guide to Triple DES. NIST withdrew it on January 1, 2024.

specs.name: SP 800-131A Rev. 3
specs.synopsis: A NIST draft that says which algorithms and key sizes stay allowed, and until when. It is a draft, not a final rule.

specs.name: RFC 5869
specs.synopsis: HKDF: a way to make keys from a shared secret with HMAC. TLS 1.3 builds its key schedule on it.

specs.name: RFC 6229
specs.synopsis: Test vectors for the RC4 stream cipher.

specs.name: RFC 7465
specs.synopsis: It forbids RC4 cipher suites in TLS.

specs.name: RFC 7748
specs.synopsis: Elliptic curves for key agreement: X25519 and X448.

specs.name: RFC 8032
specs.synopsis: EdDSA signatures on Edwards curves, which include Ed25519.

specs.name: RFC 8439
specs.synopsis: ChaCha20 and Poly1305: a stream cipher and a one-time seal, used together to lock and seal data.

specs.name: RFC 8446
specs.synopsis: The TLS 1.3 standard. It gives the handshake, the key schedule and the records.

specs.name: RFC 8996
specs.synopsis: It formally deprecates TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1.

specs.name: RFC 9449
specs.synopsis: DPoP: it ties an OAuth token to a key that the client holds, so a server can detect a replayed token.

specs.name: PKCS #1
specs.synopsis: The RSA standard: RSA keys, encryption and signatures, including the old v1.5 padding. RFC 8017 is its current text.

specs.name: PKCS#8
specs.synopsis: The file format for a private key of any algorithm. RFC 5958 is its current text.

specs.name: X9.24-3
specs.synopsis: The ANSI standard for AES DUKPT, a scheme that gives each payment its own key. ANSI sells the text.
